15.05.2024 CRLA No.248 of 2024
Hon’ble Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.
Ms. Manisha Bhandari and Mr. Druv 
Chandra, learned counsel for the appellant.
2. Mr. Lalit Sharma, learned counsel for the 
CBI. 
3. Heard. 
4. Learned counsel for the appellant/convict 
would submit that this is an appeal filed by the 
appellant/convict against the judgment and 
order dated 15.04.2024 passed by Special Judge,
CBI Dehradun in CBI Case No.09 of 2010, 
whereby the appellant/convict has been 
convicted under Section 66 of Information 
Technology Act 2000 and has been sentenced 
accordingly.
5. Admit.
6. Summon the LCR.
7. Also heard on the bail application (IA 
No.1 of 2024).
8. Learned counsel for the appellant/convict 
would submit that the appellant/convict was on 
bail during trial and he has never misused the 
liberty of bail granted to him. 
9. Learned counsel for the CBI does not 
dispute the above submissions.
10. Having considered the submissions of 
learned counsel for the parties but without 
expressing any opinion about the final merits of 
the case, in the opinion of this Court, the 
appellant/convict deserves to be enlarged on 
bail during the pendency of present criminal 
appeal.  11. Accordingly, bail application is allowed. 
Let the appellant/convict be released on 
furnishing bail bond with two sureties in the 
amount of ₹50,000/- and personal bond of the 
like amount to the satisfaction of the Court 
concerned.
12. List on 24.10.2024. 
(Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.) 
 15.05.2024
BS

34 CRLA No. 248 of 2024
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Ms. Manisha Bhandari, Advocate for 
the appellant.
Mr. Vijay Khanduri, Brief Holder for 
the State.
Mr. Jai Krishna Pandey, Advocate, 
holding brief of Mr. Piyush Garg, Advocate 
for the CBI.
In this appeal, the appellant was 
granted bail on 15.05.2024, when this 
Court ordered as follows:-
 “10. Having considered the submissions 
of learned counsel for the parties but 
without expressing any opinion about the 
final merits of the case, in the opinion of 
this Court, the appellant/convict deserves to 
be enlarged on bail during the pendency of 
present criminal appeal.
 11. Accordingly, bail application is 
allowed. Let the appellant/convict be 
released on furnishing bail bond with two 
sureties in the amount of Rs.50,000/- and 
personal bond of the like amount to the 
satisfaction of the Court concerned.”
 Now, a Modification Application No. 2 
of 2024 has been filed that the appellant 
has to get his retiral dues, but in the 
absence of the words “suspension of 
sentence” in the order granting bail, he is 
not getting those benefits.
 CBI has filed its objections. According 
to it, the application is not legally tenable 
because while granting bail, the 
suspension of sentence was not explicitly 
granted by the Court.
 In appeal, bail may be effective only if 
the execution of sentence appealed 
against is suspended. Therefore, this 
Court observes that by granting bail, the 
sentence appealed against remains in  suspension. 
 Modification application is disposed 
of accordingly.
 
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 24.07.2025
Jitendra
